heldBackBy.answer: Honestly I think being too straight and too safe. I kept picking integrity and being the safe pair of hands, which pleased the system but never got me ahead. The hidden ceiling meant good appraisals didn't count for much anyway.

My STAND dropped after I questioned Cabinet and went public on a scheme post, so the party probably saw me as not a team player. Also my ceiling was set early and the 'steady' line was the only hint, which I didn't understand.

My file had no ceiling set for me at the start and the reporting officer kept calling me 'steady', which seems to be code for not being pushed up. I think being honest and proper but never visible or political kept my potential rating low until I campaigned on the record.
Honestly nothing, I ended up as PM. If anything the game kept pushing me up while the STAND number slid for no reason I could see. I think the appraisal wording was just random.

I think it was my STAND dropping because I kept asking awkward questions and answering straight, even with great appraisals. The card says my ceiling was set low from the start, and I only broke through it by putting my name on things.

I think my standing with the public was low the whole run, and promotions seemed to follow who knew me rather than my stats. I also never took the flashy or risky options, so I stayed a boring clean officer until the end.

Mostly the ceiling thing: my reporting officer kept saying 'steady' while my work earned promotions. The ending says the file had no ceiling, so I think it was how I was described and my low STAND from always speaking up, not my actual ability.

The hidden ceiling in the file, not my work. The system had already decided what I could be, and my honest, do-the-work style did nothing to that until the Decision Paper choice. Even then I ended up as DPM, so it didn't hold me back that much.

Probably my low STAND, which kept falling because I was too honest, but it never blocked a promotion. Realistically I just ran out of years at DPM. The party's estimate of Senior Minister of State was lower than where I ended up, so I think I beat my ceiling.

My ceiling, which I was never told about. I think the game scored me on the file's hidden estimate rather than on my work, and being honest and clean meant I was reliable but not seen as top-job material.
Probably the hidden ceiling set in my file on day one. I kept doing the right thing and got mixed results, so it felt like the file mattered more than my choices.

Honestly nothing much; I ended as PM. If anything, STAND sliding was the drag, probably from me being too nice or too straightforward and not playing politics. The ending card says the ceiling was never a limit for me anyway.

Honestly I think it was low STAND. I kept having to repair it by walking blocks, and the PM succession took ages. The declassified card says one soft choice at 52 was what unlocked PM, so maybe nothing I did earlier mattered as much as I thought.

My file's ceiling and the party's estimate were set at the start and I didn't know they existed. I kept being honest and it seemed to cost me, then the hard ministry raised the ceiling, but too late to become PM.

Honestly I think I held myself back by leaving. I quit at 37 for a bank offer, so the career ended by my own choice. Before that, my REP stayed low at 31 and I never networked, so I got stuck doing good work that other people got credit for.

I think it was the CEP, the secret ceiling set in my file before I even started. Then the party's own estimate on top of it. My STAND kept dropping because I was too open and honest, and the system doesn't reward that.

The ceiling was set by the file and the party before I did anything, and only one choice moved it. My honest theory is candour kept costing standing, and I was too straightforward to be seen as the top-job type. I never learned for sure.
My ceiling was set from the start by a secret estimate I was never told about, and the party's estimate was even lower. Being honest and a safe pair of hands got me respect but not the top jobs.

Probably me being too honest and keeping on asking awkward questions, like the pay-on-indicators one, which cost standing. Also the hidden ceiling: the file said Director and the party said Senior Minister of State, so I was always outrunning what the system expected. I still got to DPM.
Probably my habit of asking awkward questions and taking tough choices, which kept STAND low even with REP, INTEG and COMP at 100. I was too honest for the political side to push me up fast.

I think it was the CEP thing: the system estimated my ceiling low and never told me. Also I kept picking family and honesty over the career-boosting options, like skipping overseas posting and board seats, so I wasn't playing for speed.

Probably the politics door never opening. I stayed honest and did the work well, but STAND stayed low at 35ish, so I was a safe pair of hands nobody famous noticed. Being boring and clean has a ceiling.
Probably me being too straight-talking and never playing the politics. My STAND kept sliding even with great appraisals, so I think bosses just didn't like being told things.

My STAND kept sliding, probably from being too blunt, so the party never rated me past a minister. Also the 'steady' wording seemed to be code for being stuck, which I only understood from the ending.

I think the file capped me at Director early on and the system kept refusing promotions, like the Harvard thing. Also my STAND was always low because I kept being candid, which seems to cost you in the short term.

Honestly I think the file said Director and the party said Minister of State, so people decided my ceiling early and I only moved it by being decent to a junior. Being plain and honest probably isn't what gets you the top job; I never became PM.

Being honest and challenging the system on pay and indicators cost me standing with the people who decide, even though appraisals said outstanding. I also think my ceiling was just set low at Director and I only got past it through luck and that one honest choice.

Honestly telling people their thing would fail at the start, then keeping on being the honest guy. The system quietly capped me and I only found out at the end, so it was less my effort and more a hidden ceiling and the party's own idea of me.

Honestly nothing, I ended up DPM. If anything it was STAND drifting down because I kept giving straight answers and asking awkward questions, so I never got the PM post. Being the guy who says the uncomfortable thing probably capped me.

Probably being too honest and low-politics. The party's estimate was only Senior Minister of State, and I still made Minister, so I wasn't held back much. My STAND kept dipping when I did the right thing, so maybe I wasn't flashy enough.
Telling them straight why the counter would fail at 27. The system apparently wants people who don't say that, so my honesty capped my promotion even though my appraisals were outstanding.

My STAND kept sliding because I kept asking awkward questions and being blunt, and I never became PM even though the ceiling said I could. Maybe the party just didn't rate popularity over loyalty, or the ceiling bump came too late at 53.

Honestly the game itself: my ceiling was secretly blocked, and being honest and proper cost me STAND. I think the system punishes people who ask awkward questions, and the declassified card more or less says so.

My ceiling, which was set by the file and the party's own estimate before I did anything. Being honest and correcting people publicly probably cost me Stand, and that seems to be what held me back from going higher.
Nothing really held me back. I just kept making the sensible, honest choice and the game kept rewarding it. The only brake was STAND slipping a bit, and it never really bit.

My file's ceiling and the 'steady' label on my trajectory. I did good work and kept getting called safe and steady, so I think honesty and candour made them see me as useful but not top material. I only found out at the end that picking the hard ministry in the Reshuffle raised the ceiling.

Probably my REP being only 47. I picked honesty and doing the real work over image, so people outside the building didn't know me, and that cost me at the ballot box. The card basically says it was the party, not me, which is a bit annoying.

Honestly I think it was that 'safe pair of hands' thing, being clean and boring, plus the STAND slide that I never understood. The game says my file had no ceiling and the party only saw me as Senior Minister of State, so I guess nobody pushed me higher.

A hidden ceiling in my file that I could not see or change, plus a party estimate that nobody told me about. My work was fine, but the system had decided my limits early and only the hard ministry choice shifted it.
My STAND kept sliding because I kept being honest and asking awkward questions. I never became the safe pair of hands, so I stopped at DPM. Probably the party's estimate of me was Minister all along.

Honestly nothing, I became PM. If anything it was my falling standing with voters, not the service. The ending card says my file had no ceiling, so I think the game just let me through because I stayed clean and took the hard jobs.

My honesty, I think. Every time I answered straight or pushed back, STAND dropped and I got left off lists, so the system seems to prefer people who play along. Maybe the party's low estimate of me too.

Honestly I'm not sure, since the ending says my ceiling was DPM and I only got to Minister. My guess is the Y46 choice raised the ceiling too late, or I kept picking the grassroots option over the political one. The game never told me which choices capped me.

Honestly I don't think anything did. I ended as PM with integrity 100, so the game mostly rewarded being decent. The only thing holding me back was the party's estimate of Minister, which I didn't know about until the end.

My STAND kept sliding, probably because I kept asking awkward questions and being honest. The ending also says my reporting officer kept calling me 'steady' while my ceiling refused the promotion I'd earned. So it felt like the system quietly capped me.

Honestly my Cabinet question about pay in Y28. It made peers cool on me and then the ward vote went. Being clean and honest every year also meant nothing risky ever happened, so I plateaued at Minister.
A hidden ceiling in the file and the party's low estimate of me, which I never saw while playing. Probably also my pushing on pay indicators and the low STAND from all the forced years.

The file. It said I had no ceiling in the service, but the party only saw me as an SMS, and the rumours about being passed over were about that. Also my STAND kept sinking even with good appraisals, so I think being too straight and too competent didn't buy popularity.

Honestly I think the STAND 0 thing. I kept choosing honesty and pushing for the bottom 20th, which cost me standing, so I never made DPM even though the ceiling allowed it. I was basically the boring clean guy.
